competitors.name: Crosta Mollica
competitors.action: Crosta Mollica launched a fresh NPD wave built around premium at-home pizza: a new Pizza Base Bianca in Sainsbury's and Tesco, plus four new pizzas including frozen SKUs on Ocado and in Tesco freezers, leaning into white-sauce, Roman pinsa, and regional Italian positioning.

competitors.name: Crosta Mollica
competitors.action: Crosta Mollica's latest accounts showed turnover up 37.2% to £67.6m, with pizza revenues up 50%, as the brand expanded retail distribution, channels, and countries, a strong proof point that premium supermarket pizza can still grow in a relatively flat category.

competitors.name: Pi00a
competitors.action: Pi00a landed on ABC's Shark Tank as a Deaf- and CODA-owned frozen pizza brand, positioning globally inspired handcrafted Neapolitan pizzas as a mission-driven premium CPG story with national audience reach and clear founder-market fit.

trends.topic: Premium frozen and take-home pizza is moving toward more specific identity rather than generic premium language
trends.magnitude: Crosta Mollica is scaling with Roman pinsa, white-sauce bases, and retailer-specific frozen placements, while Pi00a is using founder story plus globally inspired Neapolitan positioning to stand out nationally.
trends.context: For Real Dough, the useful signal is that premium alone is no longer enough. The winners keep pairing artisan cues with a sharper format, origin, or founder story that retailers and shoppers can remember fast.

breaking.headline: Premium pizza brands are winning with sharper stories, not just better ingredients
breaking.impact: Crosta Mollica is turning regional Italian specificity into retail growth, and Pi00a shows that founder-led identity can punch above its size when paired with a premium frozen format. Real Dough should keep narrowing its retail story around exactly what kind of artisan pizza it is, and why that matters in one sentence.
